_comment: Copy to core/verify_registry.json. Cards name a KEY from this file in their verify_cmd; the LOOP runs it and the output goes into the evidence. Cards never hold a command string — a worker that can write files could otherwise name its own script and have the loop run it, which is the execution right coming back through the side door.
_who: Only the operator edits this file. Workers and the auto-reviewer can neither add keys nor change them; the reviewer will suggest a key it sees here, never invent one.
_page: Front-end cards are the ones that cannot self-certify: no execution right means no machine output, so the machine-evidence gate correctly refuses them. These keys give the LOOP a way to produce that evidence. Point them at YOUR pages and YOUR assertions — one key per page is the intended shape. Needs a Chrome/Edge on the machine (doctor reports whether it found one).
_page_note: Assertions run against document.body.innerText (so <script>/<style> source never counts as page content) plus arbitrary JS expressions via --expect-js. --no-console-errors turns an uncaught exception into a red verification instead of a green one. Add --screenshot <path> to leave a picture a human can look at.
